title: CRITIC_VERIFICATION architecture hub is deleted but the pair is still claimed and linked
affected_invariant: FRZ-CTL-05 (Critic/Verification: one owner, one canonical boundary)
evidence: E1:docs/project/architecture/CRITIC_VERIFICATION.md does not exist at the baseline SHA (git log shows it deleted in cb67c363d, 2026-09-04); the plan header still says 'Architecture (1:1)' and runtime hub rows :64/:120 plus at least 10 architecture docs link to the missing file
impact: Primary-24 row #18 is a LEGACY/HISTORICAL pair with one side missing, so every link to it is broken and the 'canonical pair' rule cannot be checked mechanically. FRZ-CTL-05 is PASS (CV-VERIFIED) for 'Critic/Verification' via CTRL-X plane CX-05 while the semantic owner is now DECISION_SYSTEM/DECISION_VERIFICATION (C21), a different domain name.
recommendation: Owner to either restore a short tombstone CRITIC_VERIFICATION.md that points to DECISION_VERIFICATION, or drop row #18 and the broken links; and restate FRZ-CTL-05's owner as the Decision Verification doc.

title: Domain hubs assert enterprise certification or P3/E4 maturity that the roadmap does not contain
affected_invariant: Roadmap is the authority for formal closure (authority hierarchy); FRZ-OBS-02, FRZ-PRD-*
evidence: E1:grep of the roadmap file at the baseline SHA returned 0 matches for MEM-ENTERPRISE, OBS-FINAL, RAG-PROD/RAG-LIVE/RAG-FINAL and NPSC-3C; the MEMORY hub SHA 4db4bb69 resolves and is an ancestor of the baseline
impact: Four hubs carry domain-level certification statements (MEMORY ENTERPRISE CERTIFIED/CLOSED, OBSERVABILITY PASS - ENTERPRISE CERTIFIED, RAG A5/P3/E4 PRODUCTION_QUALIFIED_WITH_LIMITATIONS, UER FROZEN/ENTERPRISE-QUALIFIED) with no matching roadmap stage; the other 13 hubs in this batch state P2/E3 at most. OBSERVABILITY is claimed certified while all 7 FRZ-OBS rows are OPEN and RAG claims P3 while all FRZ-PRD rows are OPEN. A reader can mistake these for formal closure.
recommendation: Owner to mark these hub statements as historical or scoped (naming the roadmap stage that actually closes them: EBH-2H, EBH-2G, HARNESS-W5/TRACE-X) and to state that they are not an ARCH-FREEZE closure; Campaign B may replay the cited qualification records.

title: Eleven profile models are mirrored between Tier-0 host_profile_slices.py and Tier-3 sub_profiles.py; five have diverged field sets and no parity test was found
affected_invariant: One semantic owner per contract (FRZ-OWN-*, FRZ-CTR-*); DUP-X duplicate-mechanism certification
evidence: E1:ast comparison at the baseline SHA: 11 same-named classes in both files; identical fields for GuardrailProfile, ContextDecisionProfile, ContextProfile, ExecutionBoundaryExportProfile, ApplicationSecurityProfile, EvaluationProfile, OrchestrationProfile; diverged (app model has extra fields) for PolicyRulesProfile, MemoryProfile (17 extra), CostProfile (9 extra), ReliabilityProfile (9 extra), AdaptiveProfile; grep of tests/ and scripts/ found no parity/drift test
impact: Runtime code imports the Tier-0 slice (11 importers, e.g. reliability_runtime_bridge, profile_orchestration_resolver) while hosts configure the Tier-3 model; extra='forbid' models mean a field added only to the app model is silently absent for runtime consumers. The ORCHESTRATION hub does not name the canonical module. Only OrchestrationProfile is acknowledged as a 'legacy duplicate' (W0 guardrails); the others are acknowledged only as out-of-scope legacy coupling. DUP-X is CLOSED, so either it scoped these out or missed them.
recommendation: Owner to decide per model whether the Tier-0 slice is the canonical contract (and Tier-3 imports it) or a deliberate projection, add a parity test, and state this in the domain hubs; Campaign B can confirm DUP-X scope.

title: Five execution-path domains have no roadmap stage, no FRZ family and no control plane of their own
evidence: E1:grep of the roadmap at the baseline SHA found no stage row naming REASONING_AND_COGNITION, MODALITY, CODE_CRAFT or NEXUS_EXECUTION_FLOW; the FRZ-CTL planes (A3 data) cover Security, Reliability, Cost, Evaluation, Critic, Observability, Diagnostics, Tools, Skills, Agent Registry, Capability Graph and Context Engineering only; ORCHESTRATION and NEXUS appear only through FRZ-EXE-03 (EV-INCOMPLETE) and harness stages; CODE_CRAFT only through FRZ-SEC-05 (OPEN); none of PDC-X D1..D8 targets these domains
impact: These domains self-assess A4/I3-I4/P1-P2/E3 and several are PARTIAL (Execution-centric Nexus/Orchestration are TARGET), yet nothing in the roadmap or FRZ checklist owns their certification, so ARCH-FREEZE cannot show them as covered or explicitly out of scope. Package intergrax/runtime/nexus (328 py files) is shared by five domains and intergrax/runtime/cognition (the only package the REASONING doc owns) is a single file.
recommendation: Owner to record, for each of the five domains, either the roadmap stage/FRZ family that covers it or an explicit scoped exclusion; Campaign B to check whether HARNESS-FINAL actually covers planner/classifier and CodeCraft paths.

title: Domains with more than one owner or with owner docs that do not match the code owner
evidence: E1:ws:A8/input_A8-1.jsonl lists doc-mentioned packages that are owned by other docs (ORCHESTRATION: intergrax/distributed, intergrax/queueing belong to C18; PLATFORM_FOUNDATION lists 12 tier-example packages); PDC_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX.md is still a draft (OD-PDC-ADR-01 pending)
impact: MEMORY.md (plan pair) defers to MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md as canonical; agent lifecycle is split across AGENT_CONTRACTS_AND_ASSEMBLY, AGENT_DISTRIBUTION and the registry projection; context lifecycle across CE and UNIFIED_CONTEXT_LIFECYCLE; SKILLS has a code-level lifecycle owner but no doc section; Orchestration contract has two same-named owners (f3). Doc-mention package lists are unreliable as an ownership index. EQOA-A4 already covers the missing owner docs for tenant, security and state; not re-filed.
recommendation: Owners to name one canonical owner per row in the hubs (PDC ownership matrix is the vehicle for D1/D2/D3 rows) and to prune package mention lists to owned packages.

title: Domain hubs without tenant or security rules of their own
affected_invariant: FRZ-TEN-01..12 / FRZ-SEC-* (tenant isolation and security stated per domain)
impact: REASONING (0 tenant mentions), CONTEXT_ENGINEERING (one snippet field), PLATFORM_FOUNDATION (out-of-scope mention) state no tenant/security rules; ORCHESTRATION and SKILLS state only an authority-narrowing rule. Tenant behaviour for context assembly and planning rests on TENANT-X/CTRL-X alone, and TENANT-X/C13 and security C16 have no architecture owner doc (EQOA-A4, referenced not re-filed). Memory and RAG hubs do state tenant scoping.
recommendation: Owners to add a short tenant/security rule section or an explicit pointer to the TENANT-X record; Campaign B may sample FRZ-TEN-06 for the context path.

title: Domain hubs without a lifecycle owner or a failure/recovery owner
impact: Failure/recovery owner absent in PLATFORM_FOUNDATION, SKILLS and MEMORY and only partial in CONTEXT_ENGINEERING and MODALITY; lifecycle owner absent in LLM_ADAPTERS, REASONING, MODALITY and PLATFORM_FOUNDATION (the last is a rules domain, so acceptable). Where hubs do delegate (AGENT_CONTRACTS, ORCHESTRATION) they point to RELIABILITY_FAILURE_AND_HITL, whose C17 owner is a five-document set and whose FRZ-REL family is 11/11 OPEN.
recommendation: Owners to add a one-paragraph recovery/lifecycle pointer per hub naming the C17 or registry owner.
